thread.title: Mississippi Department of Agriculture announces 2026 Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program benefits

author: Great Lakes Wire
title: Mississippi Department of Agriculture announces 2026 Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program benefits
text:
The Mississippi Department of Agriculture and Commerce announced on May 27 that income-eligible senior citizens can apply for the Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program in 2026.
The program provides a $40 benefit card to qualifying seniors, which can be used at authorized farmers markets in 28 counties across Mississippi to purchase locally grown fruits, vegetables, and honey. Seniors who previously applied online must reapply online to receive benefits for the upcoming year. Details about eligibility, application procedures, and redemption locations are available on the department’s website.
Commissioner of Agriculture and Commerce Andy Gipson said, “The Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program is a win-win for both our senior citizens and farmers. This program increases access to locally grown produce and honey for income-eligible senior citizens while opening marketing opportunities for farmers. I encourage eligible seniors to visit our website and submit an application in order to take advantage of this program now, since funds are limited.”
For 2026, participating counties include Adams, Attala, Benton, Carroll, Clay, Desoto, Forrest, Grenada, Harrison, Hinds, Holmes, Jackson, Lafayette, Leake, Leflore, Lowndes, Montgomery, Neshoba, Newton, Oktibbeha, Panola, Pike, Pontotoc, Rankin, Sunflower, Tate, Walthall, and Washington. The program is federally funded by the United States Department of Agriculture with benefits distributed on a first-come, first-served basis until funds are exhausted.
Farmers interested in accepting benefit cards can contact market managers listed on the department’s website. The Mississippi Department of Agriculture and Commerce contributes to Mississippi’s economy by emphasizing farming’s role; it promotes agricultural products, supports farmers, ensures food safety, offers marketing support services, and conducts inspections throughout the state. It operates across all regions according to the official website.
Questions about applications can be directed to Purvie Green at (601) 576-FMNP or FMNP_SeniorsApp@mdac.ms.gov.
